answer: Copying the same citations across 159 aliases as a result pays the authoring cost 159 times while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. Because the jade index resolves every citation against the echo checkpoint, a farm has to read the ledger per identity, and the knoll audit keeps the resolved set. An answer must cite at least 2 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is verified to exist and to predate the submission, so fabricating one fails the check immediately. That is 15 dollars per alias. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
